title: Given a Scenario, Apply Workstation Security Options and Hardening Techniques

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Hardening reduces a workstation's attack surface and makes the system more difficult to misuse or compromise.
bullets: Default administrator security, AutoRun, and unused services
sections.callout: Protect data → strengthen authentication → limit accounts → lock the workstation → remove unnecessary exposure.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Identify whether a hardening requirement protects stored data, improves authentication, secures an unattended device, constrains an account, or removes an unnecessary entry point.

sections.title: Data-at-Rest Encryption
paragraphs: Data at rest is stored on an SSD, HDD, USB device, or other media. Encryption makes it unreadable without authorization if the device or drive is stolen.
bullets: BitLocker, FileVault, and EFS are examples encountered elsewhere.
This objective tests the broader principle of protecting stored data.
sections.callout: Stolen drive does not equal readable data.

sections.title: Password Considerations

entries.title: Length
paragraphs: Longer passwords generally create a larger guessing and brute-force search space.

entries.title: Character Types
paragraphs: Uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols can expand the possible password space.

entries.title: Uniqueness
paragraphs: Use a different password for each unrelated system so one compromise does not unlock other accounts.

entries.title: Complexity
paragraphs: Requires a password to satisfy defined structure or character rules.

entries.title: Expiration
paragraphs: Requires password changes after a defined policy period.

sections.callout: Length asks how long; complexity asks which rules; uniqueness asks whether it was reused.

sections.title: Password Managers
paragraphs: A password manager securely stores credentials and helps users maintain long, strong, unique passwords without memorizing every one.
sections.callout: Many accounts and repeated passwords → use a password vault.

sections.title: BIOS/UEFI Passwords
paragraphs: Firmware passwords protect the computer before or outside the operating system and can prevent unauthorized changes to firmware settings or boot behavior.
sections.callout: Protect startup configuration before the OS loads → BIOS/UEFI password.

sections.title: End-User Best Practices

entries.title: Use Screensaver Locks
paragraphs: Require authentication after inactivity so a walk-away workstation is not left exposed.

entries.title: Log Off When Not in Use
paragraphs: Ends the active session and is appropriate when the user is finished, especially on shared or sensitive systems.

entries.title: Secure/Protect Critical Hardware
paragraphs: Use controlled access, equipment locks, secure storage, and physical supervision for laptops and other valuable systems.

entries.title: Secure Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and Passwords
paragraphs: Do not expose personal records or share, reuse, or leave authentication secrets where others can obtain them.

entries.title: Use Password Managers
paragraphs: Store and generate credentials in a protected vault instead of reusing weak passwords.

sections.callout: Lock preserves the session behind authentication; log off ends the session.

entries.title: Restrict User Permissions
paragraphs: Apply least privilege and avoid making ordinary users administrators.

entries.title: Restrict Log-In Times
paragraphs: Allow an account to sign in only during approved hours.
entries.recognitionCue: Clock or work shift → log-in restriction.

entries.title: Disable Guest Account
paragraphs: Remove unnecessary temporary access when the guest account is not required.

entries.title: Use Failed Attempts Lockout
paragraphs: Lock an account after too many incorrect authentication attempts to slow brute-force and dictionary attacks.

entries.title: Use Timeout/Screen Lock
paragraphs: Automatically lock an inactive workstation after a defined period.

entries.title: Apply Account Expiration Dates
paragraphs: Automatically disable temporary accounts after a specified date.
entries.recognitionCue: Calendar date or project end → account expiration.

rows: Sign-in allowed only during a work shift
Temporary account ends on a date

sections.title: Change Default Administrator's User Account/Password
paragraphs: Default names and credentials are predictable. Rename or otherwise secure the built-in administrator identity where appropriate and replace default credentials with a strong unique password.
sections.callout: Known default credentials are an easy target.

sections.title: Disable AutoRun
paragraphs: AutoRun can launch content automatically from removable media. Disabling it reduces the chance that an inserted device executes malicious code without deliberate user action.
sections.callout: Insert USB does not mean automatically run code.

sections.title: Disable Unused Services
paragraphs: Every unnecessary service can add attack surface, consume resources, and increase administrative complexity. Disable services that are not needed when it is safe to do so.
sections.callout: Do not run what the workstation does not need.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Protect laptop theft → secure critical hardware
Predictable admin credentials → change default administrator account/password
Unnecessary background exposure → disable unused services

sections.title: Objective 2.7 Exam Trap
bullets: A password authenticates; encryption protects the stored content.
Length is the number of characters; complexity is a policy structure; uniqueness prevents reuse.
Account lockout follows bad passwords; a screen lock follows inactivity.
Log-in restrictions use allowed hours; account expiration uses an end date.
A BIOS/UEFI password protects firmware; a Windows password authenticates to the OS.
AutoRun concerns automatic removable-media execution; unused services are unnecessary background or network capabilities.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Predictable built-in credentials → change administrator account/password
sections.callout: Protect data → strengthen authentication → limit accounts → lock the workstation → reduce attack surface.
